content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'd like to share my experience controlling [product_name] using Visual Studio.NET. I developed a .NET class library (DesTransfer.dll) for communication with any [product_name] device via VB.NET. Using this library, you can: 1. Start/stop the device; 2. Monitor I/O; 3. Use ActiveX components with [product_name] HMI tools; 4. Integrate with SCADA; 5. Implement PC-based automation; 6. Enable remote device access over LAN or Internet, among other uses. I've provided sample VB.NET code and the DLL library; it should be self-explanatory, but feel free to ask questions or provide feedback. Regards

Dear Sir, I hope this message finds you well. I'm very grateful for your valuable contribution. Achieving this has always been a goal of mine, but I lacked time as I'm not a software developer. Now, thanks to your work, my vision has become reality. Congratulations, and good luck!

Hello, I appreciate your work. I'm also trying to build a homemade monitoring tool. Could you share where you found the protocol sdk? In my setup, [product_name] is used to control lighting — I want to remotely toggle outputs via PC. Is this feasible, or is monitoring the only option? Thanks for any advice.

Hi [user_name], it's possible. I recommend running your application locally and accessing it remotely using tools like TeamViewer. Just carry the program on a USB stick and use it in a public PC without needing admin rights. There are other options, but this is straightforward. You can even access your [product_name] configuration page locally. Best of luck.

Thanks, but I didn't fully understand your explanation. I'm a developer but unfamiliar with .NET like [user_name]. I want to build a simple interface to check and set output status, without giving users access to the full configuration software. To develop this, I need a protocol or SDK to communicate with [product_name], so my tool can operate it. I hope this clarifies my needs. Thanks, [user_name].

Hello [user_name], I obtained the communication protocol by reverse engineering [product_name] software. The SDK (DesTransfer.dll library) is my own and open for anyone to use, distribute, or modify. You can control and monitor any I/O, similar to the original software. For example: getRemoteIOStatus() returns all I/O as an Integer Array; writeBytes(address As Integer, writeValue() As Integer) lets you modify them. My motivation: my customer owns a sports club with an automated machine managed by [product_name] devices, without an HMI and unsynchronized with the club's PC, which tracks player stats in a SQL database. My solution installs a PC at each machine for HMI, scorekeeping, animation, payments, and statistics uploads. I'm now expanding the project for Android device control.

Nice work! I couldn't find an SDK either, so I used Ethereal to analyze my requirements. I code in Delphi and don't have time to pick up .NET or C#, but I'll try your DLL if possible. Mapping types with external DLLs can be tricky though. Appreciate your advice. Not much thanks to [company_name] for not providing any SDK. If I make progress, I'll follow up. Thanks again!
Hello [user_name], and apologies if my previous response was unclear. I consider [user_name]'s work excellent and unique. He seems very knowledgeable and generous in sharing his expertise. Good luck.
Hi [user_name], hope you're doing well. Quick question: do I need to purchase Visual Studio.NET to use your sample program? Thank you for the help.

Hello [user_name], you can download the free (Express) edition from Microsoft at [url], or run the compiled executable from the SampleLogoCommunicator/bin/Debug directory without Visual Studio.NET. Just double-click SampleLogoCommunicator.exe. Here's a screenshot of the sample program. Regards,
Thank you very much for your response, Sir. I will give it a try.

Hello [user_name], I tried your application in Visual Basic via ethernet and it works, but only for several seconds before disconnecting. After 6-7 seconds, it stops responding and shows an exception from 'DesTransfer.TXException' in DesTransfer.dll. An image of the error is attached. How can I fix the timeout?

Hi [user_name], good effort! This error is caused by a low read timeout setting. Use the following function to set read and write timeouts: setComTimeOut(readTimeOut, writeTimeOut). Both parameters are in milliseconds. For example: dTrans.setComTimeOut(3000, 1000). If the issue continues, please send me the InnerException message as shown here: Catch ex As TXException txtMessage.AppendText(ex.InnerException.Message & vbCrLf) End Try. Regards,

Hello [user_name], after changing the timeout values, the issue remains — after 6-7 seconds, communication with the device stops, even if I just change the display time. I’m only testing connection/disconnection. Could you provide example code to display the input/output statuses for the device?

Hello [user_name], to pinpoint the issue, please update your error handling code as follows: Catch ex As TXException txtMessage.AppendText("Error: " & ex.Message & " Detail Error Code : " & ex.InnerException.Message & vbCrLf) End Try. Then retry and send me the resulting message. Regards,
Hello [user_name], I am attaching images of the error messages after your suggested changes. Hope I implemented everything correctly.
Hello [user_name], I found that the application in Visual Basic mode only works for 6 seconds using [product_name] Ethernet. Error: Read Time Out Detail Error Code: DTx0108L01.

Dear Sir, I'm using your software but encountering errors when connecting over ethernet between two PCs. The error is: Failed To Connect To: No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it 127.168.0.1:10001. Thank you and regards, [user_name]

Hello, I downloaded your sample and communication works well. I also had to set dTrans.setComTimeOut(3000,1000), otherwise it stops working after 7 seconds. I’d like to make some changes: I want to monitor I/O and control outputs, but I’m not a developer and not skilled with Visual Studio. When I try getRemoteIOStatus, I keep getting the same timeout error. Updating the error code shows: Error: Read Time Out Detail Error Code: DTx0116L01. Could you help me get started? Thanks. "You can control I/O with getRemoteIOStatus() for monitoring, and writeBytes(address, writeValue) for modification."

Dear Sir, I found your sample and appreciate it. However, I’d like VB code examples for reading and writing inputs and outputs. For example, pressing a button in my app to activate a given input, and also reading current input/output states. Can you help? Thank you, [user_name]
You can use getRemoteIOStatus() to obtain I/O values as an Integer Array and writeBytes(address, writeValue) to modify them.

Dear [user_name], when using your code to control a [product_name] device, I get the error "Not Acknowledged Response From PLC" when calling getRemoteIOStatus(). Can you provide an example of how to read a specific input or set an output? Best regards, [user_name]

Dear [user_name], thank you for sharing your code — it's a significant contribution. I’ve spent a lot of time trying to control [product_name] devices with Visual Basic 6.0 through ActiveX/OCX. I’ve read others’ questions about input/output status and have encountered the same errors. Has anyone found a solution? I use Visual Basic 6.0, but it’s quite different from VB.NET, so an example of using getRemoteIOStatus to access input and output state would be appreciated. Excuse my English! Any suggestions welcome, and thank you very much.
Dear Sir, I’m trying to read and write inputs/outputs using your program but haven’t succeeded. Can you share a sample program for reading/writing data to the device? Thank you, [user_name]

Hello [user_name], your work is excellent, thanks! I'm working on my own C# .NET application using your DLL, but I ran into a few issues: First, when the [product_name] device is in stop mode, getDeviceState() returns int 2, not int 66 as expected. Second, when trying to read all I/O, my code freezes and the array remains empty. I hope you can help clarify these issues. Regards, [user_name]

I just downloaded and tested your code — it connects to [product_name], but trying to read data results in a Read Time Out error with inner exception code DTx0116L01. If I can get past this, your code would be the best solution I’ve found so far for communicating with [product_name].
Dear Sir, thanks for your .NET VB source code. My question is how to send values from [product_name] to VB.NET and how to retrieve data from [product_name].

Would you consider sharing the DLL source code? I’d be glad to help maintain and upgrade it. I have experience in concurrent and WPF programming for industrial automation and quality control lab equipment.
Which devices does your DLL support? Thanks.

Hey [user_name], I emailed you about how to toggle I/O on [product_name], and also wanted to ask if you could share the LogoCommunicator class source code. I tried dTrans.getRemoteIOStatus(), but ran into an exception. Thanks for your prompt help. Regards
Dear, did you solve your issue? I'm facing the same problem.

Dear, thanks for your work. However, I’ve encountered an issue with Ethernet: "Failed To Connect To: No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it…" Any idea how to fix this?
Hello [user_name], which [product_name] model are you using? For [version_no] the communication port is 10001; for [version_no] it's 8080.
I'm using [version_no], but the error mentions port 10001. What should I do specifically?
I'm not sure since I don’t know much about the software, but you might be connecting via the wrong port.
Thanks, but do I need to load something onto the device from its configuration software first? For example, input network or anything?
If there isn't a program loaded on the device, there’s no way for the software to access it.

Hi [user_name], I tried to use your DLL but it only works for [version_no] (port 10001), not for [version_no] (port 8080). Would you be able to add support for [version_no] users? We see errors about refused connections at IP port 10001. Regards,
For reference, [user_name] was last active on 5/2/2016.
I noticed that, but thought it was worth trying. Without the source code, there's no way to change the port from 10001 to 8080 for [version_no]. Do you know anyone who could assist?
Hi, I decompiled DESTRANS.DLL. Maybe someone can make use of it?

Hi [user_name], your solution is invaluable to me and many others. Thank you! I'm still unable to use it with [version_no], despite forcing port 8080. Is it impossible, or am I using the wrong approach? EDIT — I see it's incorrect, but is there a way to change the port?

Dear Expert, is it possible for you to contact the author of this library about the issue? It would be helpful. Has [company_name] planned to release any API for [product_name] devices? Thanks in advance.
Hello, do you have a manual for this class? LogoCommunicator and LogoCommands. I’d like to know how to access device addresses so I can interact with inputs and outputs. [user_name]
Communication doesn't work with this code due to port 10001 issues. Is there another sample C# code that solves this? Does [version_no] support snap7.dll?
For [product_name] [version_no], the communication port number is not 10001, but 8080.
Can someone try this example with [version_no] and share the results here? [url]
Can anyone explain how to change the port from 10001 to 8080? Thanks.
A new question published by [user_name] has been split to a separate thread about communicating with [product_name] [article_no] via Ethernet using VB.NET. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are keen to develop custom PC interfaces for remote monitoring and control of [product_name] devices, including I/O manipulation. The absence of an official SDK or communication protocol from [company_name] leads many to reverse engineer solutions or rely on community-driven DLLs and libraries. While these tools are appreciated, users frequently express frustration with the lack of formal documentation, official support, and simple integration methods for a range of programming languages and platforms.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope [company_name] will provide official SDKs or documentation for robust communication with [product_name] devices. They expect reliable, well-documented APIs to enable monitoring and control of inputs/outputs from their preferred development environment, ensuring easy integration and full access to device capabilities.
